sections.title: SQL: top 5 crime types and their percentages
sections.question: Write SQL to compute the top 5 crime types and their percentages.
sections.output:
SELECT i.primary_type,
       COUNT(*)                                           AS crime_count,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_total
FROM chicago_crime c
JOIN iucr i ON i.iucr_code = c.iucr_code
GROUP BY i.primary_type
ORDER BY crime_count DESC
LIMIT 5

      primary_type  crime_count  pct_of_total
             THEFT          105         21.08
           BATTERY           85         17.07
   CRIMINAL DAMAGE           49          9.84
     OTHER OFFENSE           39          7.83
DECEPTIVE PRACTICE           38          7.63

INSIGHT: The top 5 types make up 63.45% of all crimes. SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () is a window function: it puts the grand total on
         every row, before LIMIT is applied.

sections.title: SQL: arrest count per year
sections.question: Write SQL to compute arrest count per year.
sections.output:
SELECT year, SUM(arrest) AS arrest_count, COUNT(*) AS crime_count,
       ROUND(100.0 * AVG(arrest), 2) AS arrest_rate_pct
FROM chicago_crime GROUP BY year ORDER BY year

 year  arrest_count  crime_count  arrest_rate_pct
 2012             2            2           100.00
 2013             1            1           100.00
 2014             0            1             0.00
 2015             2            4            50.00
 2016           119          490            24.29

INSIGHT: 2016 has 119 arrests from 490 crimes (24.29%). arrest is stored as 0/1, so SUM gives the count and AVG gives the rate.

sections.title: Database stored views
sections.question: Create views vw_crime_yearly and vw_crime_by_category.
sections.output:
CREATE VIEW vw_crime_yearly AS
SELECT year, COUNT(*) AS total_crimes, SUM(arrest) AS total_arrests,
       ROUND(100.0 * AVG(arrest), 2) AS arrest_rate_pct, SUM(domestic) AS domestic_crimes
FROM chicago_crime GROUP BY year;

CREATE VIEW vw_crime_by_category AS
SELECT i.primary_type, COUNT(*) AS total_crimes,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_total,
       SUM(c.arrest) AS total_arrests, ROUND(100.0 * AVG(c.arrest), 2) AS arrest_rate_pct
FROM chicago_crime c JOIN iucr i ON i.iucr_code = c.iucr_code GROUP BY i.primary_type;

                  name  type
         chicago_crime table
        city_community table
      data_quality_log table
      district_ps_info table
           etl_run_log table
                  iucr table
      police_beat_info table
     summary_community table
summary_crime_category table
  summary_crime_yearly table
           ward_office table
  vw_crime_by_category  view
       vw_crime_yearly  view

INSIGHT: A view stores only the query, so it is always current; the summary tables store results and must be refreshed when the
         data changes.
